doc.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Black and white big bands compared
summary: Dance says early white bands were more polished but did not swing, and notes Basie's battered instruments and head arrangements.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Was there a difference in sound, to your ears, between most of the white bands and most of the black big bands?

Yes. Yes. I think so. I think in a sense, and you might say in the early days, the white bands were a bit more polished, but they didn’t swing. You know, that was really, I mean when Basie’s band comes out of Kansas City and there’s a sensation, George Simon, the critic said it was out of tune and everything.
